title: Building cards only state dates the records actually give
items: A card no longer says a house "had stood like this since 1904" because 1904 is the year you are visiting. That line came from the scene's own date, not from any source.

Cards now say when a building was built where a source gives it: "Built in 1886", "Built about 1832", or "Built in 1864 or 1875" where the sources disagree. 42 buildings have a sourced year so far, from the Prairie Avenue district markers and Andreas's history.
Where a source only shows a building standing, the card says so: "Recorded here by 1831", "still in 1911". Where nothing dates it, the card says nothing rather than guess.

1736 Prairie, the McBirney house, now reads "Built in 1864 or 1875": the Glessner House Museum dates it to 1864, but an 1875 building permit for the same lot may mean the house that stood there was a newer one.
